mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -1% AND HOUST < 1000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.5% in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and a decline of more than 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) over two months signals inflationary pressure combined with reduced household savings, which erodes consumer purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous by >0.5% AND RSAFS < previous by >2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such inflationary episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) cut of at least 0.5% in a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts liquidity and lowers risk premia, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) following a >=0.5% FEDFUNDS cut.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month signals a paradoxical labor market shock (e.g., mass layoffs with temporary rehiring), which increases uncertainty and reduces earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE and PAYEMS both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained sub-1% annualized GDP growth.
